summary: [Network Seminar] [Hybrid] - ECE/RBCCPS/CNI -- March 09, 2026 -- Incentive Compatibility in Two-Stage Repeated Stochastic Games
description:
Dear All,

Networks Seminar, supported by the Centre for Networked Intelligence, is a technical discussion forum in topics including but not limited to computer networks, machine learning, signal processing, and information theory. The seminar series has a webpage hosted at https://cni.iisc.ac.in/seminars/.

You are invited to the following seminar held as part of this series.

Title: Incentive Compatibility in Two-Stage Repeated Stochastic Games

Speaker: Prof. Bharadwaj Satchidanandan, Assistant Professor, IIT Madras

Time: 4:00 PM - 5:00 PM (IST)

Date: 09 March 2026

Venue: GJ Hall and Online on Zoom

Zoom link: https://us06web.zoom.us/j/83388976389?pwd=XcpO3GhLxsR14a7SVbPx33HQQa1jbt.1

Zoom Meeting ID: 833 8897 6389, Pass Code: NSSIISc

YouTube Livestream: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7MdpRcmUqSs

Webpage Link: https://cni.iisc.ac.in/seminars/2026-03-09/  <https://cni.iisc.ac.in/seminars/2026-03-09/>

Abstract: In this talk, we address mechanism design for two-stage repeated stochastic games—a setting using which many emerging problems in electricity markets can be readily modeled. We introduce the notion of dominant strategy non-bankrupting equilibrium (DNBE) which requires players to make very few assumptions about the behaviors of other players in order to employ their equilibrium strategy. Consequently, a mechanism that renders truth-telling a DNBE could be quite effective in molding real-world behavior along truthful lines. We present a mechanism for two-stage repeated stochastic games that renders truth-telling a DNBE.

Bio: Prof. Bharadwaj Satchidanandan is an Assistant Professor of Electrical Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras. Before this, he was a postdoctoral researcher at the Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems at Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), where he was hosted by Prof. Munther A. Dahleh. He obtained his Ph.D. from Texas A&M University where he was advised by Prof. P. R. Kumar. His research interests include cyber-physical systems, security, renewable energy, game theory, mechanism design, communications, control, networks, etc.
More details: https://sites.google.com/view/bsatchidanandan/home


ALL ARE WELCOME.

Thank you,
CNI Seminar Series Organizing Committee.
